§07 — Defeating Approval Laundering: Act Pinning and Successor Grants

  • URLs: 1-Call Brief (/07/brief/) · Full (/07-defeating-approval-laundering-act-pinning-and-successor-grants/) · Raw Markdown (/07.md) · Parts (3): P1 P2 P3
  • Thesis & Scope: Problem: Approval for action A can become a different action A′ at execution, and a crash can separate commit from receipt. — Proves: Pre-resume confinement, controller-fixed RequestedAct, fenced SQLite, and non-fabricating successor grants preserve act and return continuity. — Scope: Use the Confinement, Act-Pinning & Crash-Straddling Continuity Challenge on one approved mutation.
  • One Approved Mutation, Three Places to Fail: Suppose a policy approves raising one customer's credit limit from 10,000 to 25,000. The trusted controller first projects exactly that row and prepares the change. — Items: Before launch: the suspended worker's package SID, LPAC attribute, capabilities, Job membership, and current handle inventory are verified. A sentinel match or unclassified handle terminates the Job before instruction 0.
  • 1. Pre-Resume Kernel Verification: Subtopics: Exhibit 7.1 — Pre-resume kernel audit; Exclusive identity and anti-reuse; Raw LPAC attribute verification; Handle-table object identity, not numeric equality; The native spawn gate — A confined process must be inspected before instruction 0. Once the worker runs, every later control is negotiating with an already-active environment. — Items: TokenAppContainerSid must equal the owned package SID; | TokenSecurityAttributes must contain WIN://NOALLAPPPKG; | the attribute must be integer kind 2, count 1, not disabled (flags & 0x10 == 0), and nonzero.
  • 2. Controller-Brokered Model Egress: Subtopics: Authenticated local channels; The controller owns the route; Journal before dispatch; never replay uncertainty; Exhibit 7.6 — Unresolved model egress — Confined workers have no general network capability. Model access is a separate controller-owned transition, not an ambient HTTP client. For LPAC workers, the controller exposes a per-worker AF_UNIX endpoint with a restrictive ACL. — Items: exact HTTPS destination or isolated subscription CLI; | credential injection and fixed headers; | allowed models and output-token ceilings; | request/response byte limits and request budget; | project, agent, expiry, and control-epoch admission.
  • 3. Controller-Fixed RequestedAct: Subtopics: Exhibit 7.2 — RequestedAct lifecycle; Derivation; Durable fixation; Execution revalidation; Historical verification; Exhibit 7.4 — Sanitized RequestedAct record; Exhibit 7.5 — requested_act_mismatch — The act is derived from exact projected bytes before the worker environment is issued. It is not re-read from live model prose at execution time. This is the strict confined-worker staging path. — Items: environment ID and worker; | staging actor and complete task binding; | exact source projection receipt; | source generation and source tenancy; | the controller-fixed destination.
  • 4. §08 — The Sovereign Kill Switch: Break-Glass Epochs and the Conformance Gate

  • URLs: 1-Call Brief (/08/brief/) · Full (/08-sovereign-kill-switch-break-glass-epochs-and-conformance-gate/) · Raw Markdown (/08.md) · Parts (4): P1 P2 P3 P4
  • Thesis & Scope: Problem: A kill switch the agent can clear is not a boundary, and a green build does not prove the release enforces refusals. — Proves: Latch-first containment, scoped epochs, observed Job termination, in-doubt recovery, and the 45-case candidate gate close the loop. — Scope: Use the Break-Glass & Conformance Qualification Challenge on one containment or release requirement.
  • One Stop, Three Races, No Invented All-Clear: Suppose a safety monitor engages a machine stop after an autonomous worker begins behaving anomalously. Three races now matter, and none can be resolved by a dashboard toggle: A project-scoped stop follows the same latch and… — Items: Containment races cleanup. The latch reaches durable storage before AINA attempts to terminate owned runs or cancel queued wakes. One worker termination remains unconfirmed; the latch still closes new effects.
  • 1. Asymmetric Containment: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.1 — Stop versus recovery authority — The emergency interface deliberately gives stop and recovery different authority. Any admitted caller may invoke engage because refusal to stop is the more dangerous default. A nonempty reason is mandatory. — Items: No MCP session. If session::current() exists, recovery is refused. A model-connected tool session cannot satisfy the owner surface. | Explicit operator identity. The caller must supply --by operator; a worker or agent name is insufficient.
  • 2. Latch-First Containment: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.2 — Publication before cleanup; Exhibit 8.3 — Sanitized scoped latch record; Owned Jobs must be observed stopped; “Latched” is not the same as “fully reconciled” — An emergency stop must not depend on a database, a live server, a lease sweep, a successful process kill, or a final audit write. Those steps can fail precisely when containment is needed. The distinction matters. — Table Data: KILLING: An affected owned Job is not yet observed quiescent, a Job census failed, or a live server does not implement the current break-glass observation protocol. | RECONCILING: Quiescence and protocol coverage are established, but an unresolved file, destination, or model operation remains—or its registry cannot be read.
  • 3. Control Epochs Revoke Authority, Not Just Processes: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.4 — Scoped revocation map; WAL before snapshot; Exhibit 8.5 — Sanitized epoch-advance record — A latch closes new-effect gates immediately. Control epochs handle a different problem: authority that was minted before the stop must not remain usable after the relevant boundary advances. — Table Data: Resource lease; Carried lineage: Lease.control_epoch; Recheck at the boundary: validate_tenancy checks expiry, current generation, and matching scope revision | Room wake job; Carried lineage: sealed control_epoch; Recheck at the boundary: Dispatch re-derives task/Room/project standing and refuses revoked lineage | Result-grant receiving tenancy; Carried… — Items: Reads the current epoch and per-scope revisions. | Computes next = prior + 1, refusing integer exhaustion. | Appends an epoch_advance record to breakglass.wal.jsonl and flushes it. | Atomically rewrites epoch.json with the new sequence and scope map.
  • 4. Managed Drain and In-Doubt Recovery: Subtopics: Recovery starts with a census, not amnesia; Exhibit 8.6 — Recovery intent preserves uncertainty; Stop beats recovery on a race; Exhibit 8.7 — Racing stop leaves FROZEN_SAFE — Immediate engage is not the only controlled-stop mode. drain supports a bounded window in which already durably prepared effects may finish. — Items: unresolved_file_operations() for protected file writes without an established outcome; | destinations::unresolved_operations() for nonterminal destination mutations; | model_egress::unresolved() for brokered model requests whose provider-side outcome is unsettled.
  • 5. The Candidate-Binary Publication Gate: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.8 — Candidate qualification sequence; The complete 45-case inventory — Containment architecture is only as credible as the binary that implements it. A green build proves compilation. It does not prove that the release artifact refuses stale generations, impersonation, cross-project reads, altered proposals,… — Table Data: 1; Emitted case ID: impersonation_refused; What must hold: A bound session cannot act as another owner. | 2; Emitted case ID: altered_proposal_conflict; What must hold: Reusing an operation ID with a different payload is refused. | 3; Emitted case ID: stale_generation_refused; What must hold: An edit fencing an old ownership generation is rejected.
  • 6. What the Gate Proves—and What It Cannot: Subtopics: Exhibit 8.9 — Publication summary shape — The release gate closes an important bootstrapping hole.
